item.title: 49ers' Nick Bosa clarifies ‘pure' intention behind Mexico City cheering comments
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Lee Chan

media:content.media:title: Minnesota Vikings v San Francisco 49ers
media:content.media:description: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO – NOVEMBER 22: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers interacts with fans after the 35-10 win against the Minnesota Vikings at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Agustin Cuevas/Getty Images)

item.excerpt: Star 49ers edge rusher Nick Bosa clarified his comments about fans who were planning to attend San Francisco's game in Mexico City.
item.description:
SANTA CLARA — On Wednesday, Nick Bosa clarified his intentions behind comments about the fans that were planning to attend the 49ers’ Week 11 game in Mexico City.

“I thought it was good,” Bosa said Wednesday about his reception at Estadio Banorte, which included some boos pregame. “I definitely didn’t mean any harm with my comments, but the environment was amazing like it was the last time we were there.”

Prior to the contest, Bosa suggested that information be given to fans in attendance to know when to cheer in order to create a true home-field advantage at Estadio Banorte. 

“I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer,” Bosa said last week while in Colorado Springs. “Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them, no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques, but if they can cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great.”

Turns out the NFL and the 49ers had Bosa’s back. There were explicit instructions in in both English and Spanish explained by on-field hosts M.J. Acosta and John Sutcliffe. The two reporters explained the chants to be yelled for first downs, to be quiet once the offense is preparing for the next play and to get loud while the defense is on the field. 

There also were announcements throughout the game accompanied by written instructions on the play screens. 

Bosa shared that he felt like the crowd clearly gave the 49ers an advantage, with very loud cheering while he and the defense were on the field, which was the point of his comments. 

“The intentions were pure,” Bosa said. “All the interactions that I had face-to-face were were amazing.” 

The All-Pro pass rusher shared that he was surprised by the backlash over his comments. Bosa, who is not regularly on social media during the season, was informed by his teammates who gave him a hard time, in a joking way, about the situation. 

The Ohio State product eventually saw some of the comments online, which is what prompted him shaping his hands in the form of a heart during the pregame festivities. 

With the help of everyone in attendance, Bosa’s mission was accomplished.
